title: hosted-api-quickstarts-pricing-experiments
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working messaging brief + experiment plan for the Hosted API's developer-focused quickstart funnel and price-language variants. Goal: find copy and onboarding steps that lower time-to-first-success (TTFS), increase dev signups->api-keys->first-100-tokens usage, and limit early pricing friction.

Where we are now (quick summary):
- Hosted API onboarding is fast but conversion dropoff occurs at the billing screen and first-paid-call milestone.
- Developers respond to performance and integration examples more than abstract scale claims.
- Competitors emphasize model breadth or low headline price; we should emphasize predictable cost + production-ready dev ergonomics.

Primary hypotheses to test:
1) Replace sticker-price messaging with a predictable cost framing (e.g., "estimated cost for 1k requests") reduces billing dropoff by 18–25%.
2) A 3-minute Quickstart app (sample repo + one-click deploy) increases TTFS and first-100-token calls by 30% versus code-only quickstart.
3) Transparent latency + cost per token metrics on the quickstart page increases trust and reduces support contacts.

Target metrics (what we'll measure):
- Signup -> API key created: baseline 68% -> target 75%
- API key created -> first successful token call (within 48h): baseline 42% -> target 60%
- Billing/upgrade opt-in rate after free credit: baseline 12% -> target 18%
- Support/contact rate during quickstart: reduce by 20%

Developer-first value props (short bullets to A/B):
- "Start in minutes: example app + SDKs for Node/Python, no infra required."
- "Predictable unit economics: clear per-request and per-embedding cost estimates for your traffic profile."
- "Production-grade latency: verified p95/median for common prompt sizes in our model catalog."
- "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private — move from prototype to production without rewrite."

Quickstart angles (content + UX experiments):
A. Code-first: minimal web page showing two code snippets (Node + Python), 'copy and run' flow, inline results.
B. App-first: one-click deploy sample (Vercel/Heroku) that shows an integration example (chat widget / summarizer).
C. Prompt-playground-first: interactive page where devs paste a prompt, choose model, see tokens & cost estimate update live.

Pricing-language experiments (3 variants):
Variant 1 — "Transparent pricing":
- Hero: "Pay by token. Know your cost up front."
- Inline copy: "We estimate this request costs ~$0.0008 (50 tokens). Adjust batch size or model for cost/perf tradeoffs."
- CTA: "See your estimated bill"

Variant 2 — "Developer credits & predictable bill":
- Hero: "Free credits to build. Predictable costs to scale."
- Inline: "Get $200 in credits to experiment. After credits, charges are per-token with quantity discounts and a daily usage cap you can toggle."
- CTA: "Claim credits and start"

Variant 3 — "Value-first pricing":
- Hero: "Engineered for production economics"
- Inline: "Optimize cost with caching, batching, and our recommended model profiles. We'll show you the expected cost per 1k responses for common use cases."
- CTA: "Estimate my use case"

Sample hero lines to test (short list):
- "A dev-first API for production LLMs"
- "From prototype to production — same API, fewer surprises"
- "Start for free. Ship predictable LLM features."

Email/subject-line tests for onboarding drip:
- S1: "Welcome — Your quick sample app is ready (1-click deploy)"
- S2: "See the estimated cost of your first 100 calls"
- S3: "3-minute tutorial: add a chat to your app"

Competitive notes (short):
- Vendor A: low headline price + many consumer-focused demos. Weakness: poor observability, no dedicated capacity offer.
- Vendor B: strong enterprise SLAs and private deployment. Weakness: onboarding friction, heavy sales motion.
- Vendor C: open-source model hosting toolkits (self-host). Strength: full control; Weakness: ops burden.

How we differentiate (copy + feature hooks):
- Emphasize 'developer velocity + production economics' not just low price.
- Show side-by-side: expected latency and token cost for common prompts (e.g., 256-token summarization) — this is unique and actionable.
- Highlight SDKs, examples, and one-click deploys that get you to a live demo quickly.

Objections & suggested rebuttals (for sales/CS):
- "What if my traffic spikes?" -> "We have autoscaling and routing policies; you can pin capacity or allow bursting. We'll also show cost forecasts for spikes."
- "How accurate are the cost estimates?" -> "Estimates are based on historical token distributions and model profiles; we include conservative buffers and show ranges."
- "How is this cheaper than X?" -> "Compare unit economics after factoring caching/ batching/quantization — we'll run a quick cost model with your sample traffic."

A/B test plan (minimum viable):
- Population: new dev signups over 4 weeks, n approx 4k signups.
- Cells: control (current flow), A (Transparent pricing copy + code-first quickstart), B (Developer credits + app-first quickstart), C (Value-first + prompt-playground).
- Primary metric: API key -> first-successful-call within 48h. Secondary: billing upgrade opt-in.
- Run length: 4 weeks or until 500 successful key->call conversions per cell.

Implementation notes / dependencies:
- Need sample app repo (GH PR linked): https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/78 (Marcus owns)
- Console: surface estimated cost calculator feature (engineering ticket: GT-494)
- SDK snippets: sync with devex (Priya) to reduce friction in copy.

Launch timeline (high-level):
- Week 0–2: finalize copy variants + build 1-click sample app
- Week 3: instrument analytics and cost-estimator on quickstart page
- Week 4–8: run A/B test, weekly check-ins, iterate based on early signals

Open questions / decisions needed (short):
- Do we give credits automatically or require a credit-card-on-file? tradeoff: friction vs abuse. (owner: Marcus)
- Which default model to show in the prompt-playground? small cost-optimized vs balanced latency. (owner: Applied ML)
- Should we expose a daily spending cap toggle in the quickstart? Ops implications. (owner: Product)

Notes / ideas to keep but not for initial run:
- Offer an "estimator wizard" that ingests sample logs and projects cost/back-of-envelope infra needs.
- Bake a short live demo in the signup email (animated gif + CTA to deploy).

People to ping in Slack:
- #g2m-hosted-api, #devex, #product-hosted-api, @marcus, @priya

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finalize hero & three pricing copy variants (Evelyn)
- Prioritize engineering tickets GT-494 and GH example PR review (Marcus)
- Draft email drip templates for the three paths (Diego)

References and internal links:
- Confluence: Hosted API launch notes (linked above)
- Linear: GTM-1123 (experiment tracking)
- GitHub: examples PR/one-click app (linked above)

Rough notes / scratch (for posterity):
- Try to avoid words like "cheap" or "low-price" in hero. Use "predictable", "estimate", "optimize" instead.
- Emphasize measurable outcomes: "ship a chat, summarize docs, embed search" as sample blueprints.
- For enterprise flows, shift messaging later in funnel to capacity, SLAs, VPC options.

End of draft.

Unresolved: need legal review on how we present "estimates" vs billed amounts before public copy (tagging security/compliance).
